articles.title: IPL media rights: Industry seeks best price-discovery models
articles.summary: Cricket News: Last week, the ICC sounded the media-rights bugle by appointing a five-member working group. The group’s top priority in the coming months will be to .
articles.body: Last week, the ICC sounded the media-rights bugle by appointing a five-member working group. The group’s top priority in the coming months will be to consider all possible steps that can help the ICC retain the existing value for the 2028-31 cycle, or even better it, by exploring the best price-discovery models available. The ICC’s media-rights tender, however, will not be the first to hit the market. The world governing body will have to wait for the BCCI to first draft and release the IPL media-rights tender, following which any other property around the world, including the ICC, will come up for sale.Meanwhile, the BCCI is yet to act on it. The Indian cricket administration, usually considered a sleeping giant unless woken from its slumber, hasn’t taken a call yet on bringing a financial agency on board to figure out the right price-discovery models, as it did during the previous rights cycle. Interestingly, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia is on the ICC media rights working group, which ECB chief Richard Thompson is heading and also includes ICC chairman Jay Shah.In 2022, the cricket board brought in financial advisory firm KPMG to draft the IPL tender document. This document included a special non-exclusive digital-rights package designed for selling a select ‘bouquet’ of high-value matches in the Indian subcontinent. Set at 18 matches per season for a 74-game structure, this package alone rose to Rs 3,273 crore at Rs 33.24 crore per game and ensured Internet rights ended up generating more revenue for the BCCI from the subcontinent for the first time in history than the traditional sale of TV rights.“We were expecting to hear something from them (BCCI) on this. Given the way tech is changing how we consume sport, we thought the board would be keen to explore these changing revenue patterns and models for IPL. Look at the YouTube sports-bundling model in the US, for instance. The NFL Sunday Ticket is a case study in itself,” said an industry executive.Sports industry executives strongly believe that the value can be tremendous if the BCCI explores this space in greater detail. The BCCI members will be in Mumbai starting on Friday for the AGM. Those tracking developments can’t think of a more important subject the members may need to discuss than the upcoming sale of media rights.“India has a strong cricket platform. The IPL is already a premium property on that platform. All you need to build on it is effectively what can be done outside of the live match feed. Archives, highlights, documentaries, regional storytelling, fan engagement etc. You may have one or two broadcasters in the race for rights but building a separate non-live consumer base to monetise premium properties selectively is another subject matter altogether,” the executive added.The key aligning principle here must be based on a modular concept, rather than the all-inclusive one that currently prevails. “Perhaps not a very healthy model either, considering all your eggs happen to be in one single basket,” says an IPL franchise executive, referring to IPL’s heavy leaning on JioStar for live broadcasts. OTT giant Netflix hasn’t majorly dabbled with the idea of putting live sport behind its paywall. However, it has certainly not backed away from exploring events that can be included within its existing plans to create a reason for people to remain subscribed.“We keep wondering why an Amazon or a Netflix or a YouTube hasn’t looked at the India market. Well, the fact is, the onus lies on us to market our products to them and only then can we catch their attention. So, in the case of IPL rights, the onus certainly lies on the BCCI to go out and start talking to these platforms,” the franchise executive added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Clear message’ for Hardik Pandya: Gautam Gambhir reveals what the all-rounder must do to return to Team India
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through gam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through game time, with the all-rounder currently not part of India's squads after not playing enough cricket since the IPL.Following India's 127-run win over Afghanistan in the third T20I in New Delhi on Thursday, Gambhir said Pandya's immediate priority should be getting back on the field, including through the India A series, before pushing for a return to the senior sides."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs, and he hasn't played a lot of cricket since the IPL, so we don't want to push him into international cricket because international cricket can be extremely tough on your body as well," Gambhir said during the post-match press conference.The India head coach also revealed that the message to Pandya has been straightforward: play, regain match fitness and then push for a place in both white-ball squads."And that was the clear message to him that if he can play that India A series, and then if everything goes well, he can come back and be part of the T20s and the one-day squad as well," Gambhir said.India could play Hardik and Nitish togetherGambhir's comments also highlighted India's plans to develop more than one seam-bowling all-rounder. Nitish Kumar Reddy, initially included in India's 15-member Asian Games squad, has been withdrawn from the continental event and will instead feature in the ODI series against the West Indies.Gambhir believes the move will give Reddy valuable game time and accelerate his development with the ball ahead of India's future assignments."From Nitish's point of view, it's actually a great thing that he's been withdrawn from the T20 format, and he'll get game time against the West Indies as well," he said. "We know how important a seam-bowling all-rounder will probably be in a year and when we go to South Africa. And once Hardik comes back, obviously it's going to be good."The coach even suggested India could eventually accommodate both Pandya and Reddy in the same playing XI."Sometimes we could even go on to play both of them in the playing 11," Gambhir said, while stressing that Pandya's current bowling workload remains a factor."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs," he added.Reddy's bowling development excites GambhirGambhir was encouraged by Reddy's progress as a seam-bowling all-rounder and believes having multiple players who can contribute with both bat and ball will give India greater flexibility."I think it's good that we got Nitish now from the Asian Games so that now he can, and you could see the more he bowls, the better he becomes, and we have when you can develop a couple of seam-bowling all-rounders, it will always be handy," Gambhir said.Reddy will now get an opportunity to feature in the ODI series against the West Indies rather than the Asian Games, providing him with additional match exposure.Abhishek's hundred powers India to 3-0 sweepThe Hardik discussion came after India completed a commanding 3-0 T20I series sweep over Afghanistan. Abhishek Sharma smashed a record-breaking 108 off just 34 balls as India posted 221/7 in the third match in New Delhi.Ravi Bishnoi and Reddy then claimed three wickets each as Afghanistan were bowled out for 94, their lowest total against India in T20Is and their heaviest defeat in the format.Gambhir, however, said the focus inside the dressing room remained on impact rather than individual milestones."I can sit here and keep talking about his 100, but it's just the impact. The only thing we talk about in that dressing room is how much impact we create with the bat and how much impact we can create with the ball," Gambhir said.India's 100 runs in the powerplay was another major positive for Gambhir."T20 cricket is not about runs or wickets; it's about how much impact you can create," he said. "The biggest positive was we got a 100 in the powerplay that we have never done in my coaching tenure."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mohammad Rizwan approaches ICC Anti-Corruption Unit over mobile phone seizure by Pakistan's cyber crime agency
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles following Pakistan’s England tour have taken another turn, with the wicketkeeper-batter approaching the ICC’s Anti-Corrupti.
articles.body: Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles following Pakistan’s England tour have taken another turn, with the wicketkeeper-batter approaching the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU) for clarity over the seizure of his mobile phone by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). The move comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed his petition challenging the agency’s notices, leaving the Pakistan cricketer seeking answers over the handling of his device and the procedures followed during the ongoing inquiry.According to sources quoted by Geo News, Rizwan submitted an online request through the ICC ACU portal, asking whether the ICC or the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) was aware of, or involved in, the action taken against him.Rizwan seeks clarity over ICC anti-corruption proceduresSources said Rizwan’s request was not intended as a complaint against any individual or organisation. Instead, the Pakistan batter has sought clarification on the procedures followed in his case and the role, if any, of the ICC or ECB in the seizure of his mobile phone.The former Pakistan white-ball captain has also asked whether the process of requesting his phone, transferring it from England to Pakistan and conducting a forensic examination was in accordance with the ICC Anti-Corruption Code.Rizwan has further sought guidance on his responsibilities and the steps he should follow while cooperating with anti-corruption authorities in the future.Lahore High Court dismisses Rizwan’s petitionThe development comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed Rizwan’s petition challenging notices issued to him by the NCCIA. During Thursday’s hearing, Rizwan’s lawyer, Qazi Umair Ali, told Chief Justice Aalia Neelum that the cricketer had been called to a hotel lobby after the Lord’s Test in England and questioned without being served a notice.According to his counsel, Rizwan’s mobile phone was taken into custody after he was assured that it would be returned within three hours. However, the device has not yet been returned.Rizwan’s lawyer also questioned the NCCIA’s jurisdiction, arguing that the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit was the appropriate forum for matters involving alleged corruption-related violations by cricketers. The court directed Rizwan to respond to the NCCIA’s notice before dismissing his petition.NCCIA probe linked to betting and alleged dressing-room leaksThe NCCIA notice relates to an inquiry into online betting and gambling in Pakistan cricket. Reports have also linked the investigation to alleged leaks of information from the Pakistan dressing room during the Test series against England.Rizwan and fellow batter Imam-ul-Haq appeared before the agency in Lahore earlier this month as part of the investigation.No final findings against Rizwan or Imam have been officially announced.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shree Charani’s four-for, Shafali's quick 40 help India beat Japan in Asian Games quater-finals
articles.summary: Cricket News: India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their pl.
articles.body: India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their place in the semi-finals against Bangladesh.The result also sets up a repeat of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 semi-final line-up, with Sri Lanka set to face Pakistan in the other last-four clash.Shree Charani stars as Japan are bowled out for 57After winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers dismantled Japan’s batting line-up, restricting the hosts to just 57 in 19.5 overs. Shree Charani led the charge with a remarkable spell of 4/10, including two maiden overs, to register the best bowling figures by an Indian at the Asian Games. Shafali Verma also chipped in with two wickets for 13 runs.Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 off 47 balls, but the hosts struggled to build partnerships against India’s disciplined attack.Shafali and Richa wrap up chase in five oversIndia’s chase was emphatic, as they reached the target in just five overs, finishing at 59/2 and winning with 90 balls to spare. Shafali Verma set the tone with a blistering 40 off 15 balls, striking six fours and two sixes. She hammered four boundaries in the opening over and later sealed the victory with a six off Shimako Kato.India had promoted Kamalini and Fulmali up the order, but the move did not pay off, with Kamalini dismissed for a duck and Fulmali scoring six. Shafali then combined with Richa Ghosh, who came in at No. 4, to complete the chase in a hurry.The pair shared a warm hug after the winning hit before crossing over to greet the Japanese players. Japan’s two wickets offered a small positive from an otherwise difficult outing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
